newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - ABARE sees sheep meat prices dampened by beef.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - ABARE sees sheep meat prices dampened by beef.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultral and Resource Economics (ABARE) said it expects average saleyard prices for Australian mutton to fall by 10 percent to A$0.60 per kg in 1996/97.
Meanwhile, lamb prices are expected to be largely unchanged at around A$2.02 per kg, ABARE said in its quarterly review published on Tuesday.
"The expected decline in mutton prices is mainly a result of weaker consumer and processor demand offsetting a slight expected tightening in domestic supply," ABARE said.
Domestic demand for sheep meat is also expected to be affected by significamtly lower retail prices for beef and veal.

However, Australian producers are expected to benefit from reduced competition in export markets, given the forecast decline in shipments of sheep meet from New Zealand, the world's largest exporter of lamb, ABARE said.

The United States, the largest market for Australian lamb, is experiencing a shortage of domestic lamb, so import demand for sheep meat is expected to remain strong, particularly for chilled lamb cuts, the forecaster added.
